title: Applied ML: Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Model Onboarding, Quality Guardrails & Regression Triage Playbook (2026)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose:
This document codifies Redwood's applied-ML evaluation and quality workflows: the eval harness, prompt set and benchmark guidance, model onboarding checklist, quantization profile process, and the regression triage playbook. It is intended for ML engineers, applied researchers, and platform owners who onboard models to serving and maintain output quality over time.

Scope:
Applies to: hosted API, Dedicated, and Private model onboarding flows; continuous evaluation runs in CI and nightly jobs; any model variant used in production (float, quantized, distilled). Does not replace security/compliance signoffs.

Related pages:
- confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/model-onboarding-eval-harness-and-guardrails-playbook-2026.json
- confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks-guidelines-2026.json

Ownership and Roles:
- Eval harness owner: applied-ml (primary) — Aisha Patel
- Model onboarding owner: model-onboarding team — Marco Chen
- Regression triage lead: SRE & applied-ml — Lena Gomez
- Quantization profiles: infra-optimizations — Ravi Kumar

Key SLOs and thresholds:
- Baseline acceptance: new model must not drop primary metric by >1.5% relative compared to the pinned baseline on the canonical benchmark suite.
- Embedding drift: mean cosine similarity to baseline embedding set must not decrease by more than 0.02 (absolute).
- Latency regression: p95 generation latency must not increase by >10% on representative traffic shape.
- Resources: quantized model memory and GPU utilization must be within the quant profile target ±10%.
- Regression alerting: any CI/nightly run that fails metric thresholds triggers the regression triage playbook.

Eval harness overview:
Intro and goals:
- Provide deterministic, reproducible evaluation runs across prompt sets, metrics, and model variants.
- Support unit, integration (CI), and scheduled (nightly) runs.
- Emit machine-readable outputs (JSON + CSV) and human-facing summary reports (HTML).

Primary components:
1) Runner: python package eval_harness.run that loads models, datasets, prompt templates, and metrics.
2) Datasets: standardized prompt sets stored under eval_assets/prompt_sets/*.jsonl.
3) Metrics: modular functions (exact_match, rouge, f1, embedding_cosine_mean, perplexity) with consistent preprocessing.
4) CI integration: GitHub Actions + nightly Airflow job that runs the core suites.

Typical commands:
- Local dev run:
  python -m eval_harness.run --model-path <model-dir> --prompt-set eval_assets/prompt_sets/saas-chat-1000.jsonl --metrics exact_match,embedding_cosine_mean --out results.json

- CI run (example in .github/workflows/eval.yml):
  - name: Run eval-harness
    run: |
      python -m eval_harness.run --model-id $MODEL_ID --prompt-set eval_assets/prompt_sets/comprehensive-2026.jsonl --metrics all --out results/$MODEL_ID.json

Prompt sets and benchmark design:
Principles:
- Representativeness: each prompt set should reflect real product workloads and extremes (edge cases).
- Determinism: store prompts as JSONL with fixed seed for any stochastic evaluation.
- Versioning: prompt set files must include metadata fields: name, created_at, owner, dataset_version.

Prompt set categories and examples:
- Sanity / smoke: 50 examples, fast, used in PR hooks.
- Canonical benchmarks: 1k-10k examples covering core user intents (e.g., saas-chat-10k.jsonl).
- Stress / long context: datasets targeting long sequence and memory behavior.
- Safety and hallucination tests: adversarial prompts for inappropriate content and factuality checks.

Creating a new prompt set (procedure):
1) Draft JSONL file in eval_assets/prompt_sets/ with header metadata.
2) Run local validation: `python -m eval_harness.validate_prompts path/to/file.jsonl`.
3) Open PR against repository with description, owner, and intended use.
4) Reviewer runs canonical suite and signs off.

Benchmark metrics and calibration:
Recommended primary metrics (choose 1-2 per workload):
- Generation tasks: BLEU/ROUGE/F1 as appropriate, and human-eval for qualitative checks.
- Question answering/fact recall: Exact Match / F1.
- Embedding tasks: mean cosine similarity and downstream clustering ARI.
- Safety / toxicity: safety-score (0-1) using internal classifier and false-positive/negative analysis.

Calibration: maintain a pinned baseline model (baseline_model_id) for each workload. Benchmarks must report relative delta to the baseline and confidence intervals (bootstrap 1000).

Model onboarding checklist:
Pre-onboarding (author):
- Add model artifact to model-registry with metadata: architecture, tokenizer, training data notes, quantization support.
- Create an onboarding PR that includes the model ID, owner, and expected cost/latency profile.

Onboarding steps (owner):
1) Run full eval harness against canonical prompt sets (smoke + canonical + safety).
2) Produce results JSON and human-readable report.
3) Confirm SLOs: quality delta ≤1.5% and latency p95 within expected.
4) If quantized variant will be used, run quantization profile process (see below) and include quant metrics.
5) Update model catalog entry with evaluation artifacts and the recommended serve config (batch size, kv-cache settings, quant profile).
6) Schedule canary rollout: 1% traffic for 48 hours, observe quality and telemetry.

Required artifacts for merge:
- results/<model_id>.json (eval outputs)
- report/<model_id>-summary.html
- model-catalog entry updated with `onboarded_at` and `onboarded_by` fields

Quantization profiles and validation:
Purpose: ensure quantized models preserve quality while meeting memory/throughput goals.

Profiles: stored under eval_assets/quant_profiles/*.yaml with fields: profile_name, method (e.g., 4-bit LLM.int8(), PTQ), calibration_dataset, expected_memory, tolerances.

Validation steps:
1) Build quantized artifact with reproducible snapshot (git hash of quant tooling).
2) Run eval_harness with identical prompt sets comparing float vs quantized variant.
3) Check thresholds: primary metric delta ≤1.5% (or absolute 0.02 embedding); memory within profile ±10%.
4) If failure: try alternate quant scheme, LORA-aware quant, or fall back to higher-bit profile.

Example quant profile (text YAML):
profile_name: low-memory-4bit
method: awq-4bit
calibration_dataset: eval_assets/prompt_sets/calibration-2k.jsonl
expected_memory_gb: "7.5"
metric_tolerance: "1.5%"
owner: infra-optimizations

Regression triage playbook:
Triggering events:
- CI/nightly eval shows metric delta beyond thresholds.
- Canary or production telemetry shows quality degradation (user complaints, error budgets, automated monitors).

Initial triage (minutes 0-30):
1) Pager + Slack alert to applied-ml and SRE oncall.
2) Collate failing reports: results JSON path, prompt examples with regression, model_id, commit hash, and serving config.
3) Re-run the eval locally against the pinned baseline and the new artifact to confirm the regression is reproducible.

Hypothesis generation (30-120 minutes):
- Is this caused by model artifact change (weight deltas)? Compare checksums and training notes.
- Is it caused by tokenization differences? Run tokenizer diff tool: `python -m eval_harness.tokenizer_check --model-a A --model-b B --examples 100`.
- Is it a serving config regression? Compare batch sizes, kv-cache settings, temperature, sampling seeds.
- Was a quantization profile applied improperly? Compare float vs quantized results.

Mitigation and remediation (2-24 hours):
- Rollback: if production impact is severe and root cause unknown, rollback to previously pinned model via the rollout controller.
- Hotfix: if the regression is config related, deploy config change (e.g., revert sampling hyperparam) and re-run canary.
- Re-evaluation: if model quality regressed due to upstream training changes, open a model-release ticket and halt rollout until a fix or retraining is completed.

Postmortem and action items (24-72 hours):
1) Write a short incident summary in confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems with reproduction steps and the minimal repro prompt set.
2) Add failing prompts to a quarantined prompt set for future guarding.
3) Update eval harness: add new regression test (smoke or canonical) to CI where appropriate.
4) If quantization or tooling bug caused regression, create infra ticket and assign to owner.

Diagnostics and tooling (useful commands):
- Run reproducible eval for a single prompt: `python -m eval_harness.run --model-id M --prompt-file prompts/single.jsonl --metrics all --out /tmp/repro.json`
- Compare results: `python -m eval_harness.compare results/baseline.json results/candidate.json --report diff.html`
- Tokenizer diff: `python -m eval_harness.tokenizer_check --model-a baseline --model-b candidate --examples 100`
- Generate HTML summary: `python -m eval_harness.report results/candidate.json --template templates/summary.html --out report/candidate.html`

Configuration and example table:
Item | Location / Example | Notes
canonical prompt sets | eval_assets/prompt_sets/* | Versioned and PR-driven
quant profiles | eval_assets/quant_profiles/*.yaml | Owned by infra-optimizations
CI workflow | .github/workflows/eval.yml | PR smoke + nightly canonical runs
baseline tracking | model-catalog/baselines.json | baseline_model_id + pinned date

Governance and review cadence:
- Prompt sets: reviewed quarterly and after any major product change.
- Canonical benchmark suite: reviewed annually or on major model-family change.
- Quant profiles: validated per release and on infra changes (CUDA/tooling updates).
- Regression triage: postmortem and corrective actions tracked in Jira and reviewed in the monthly reliability retro.

Appendix: example eval JSON schema (summary fields):
- model_id (string)
- run_id (string)
- prompt_set (string)
- metric_primary (string)
- metric_primary_value (number)
- metric_baseline_value (number)
- delta_relative_pct (number)
- p95_latency_ms (number)
- memory_gb (number)
- quant_profile (string or empty)
- run_timestamp (ISO8601)

Additions and feedback:
If you find gaps in the harness or prompt sets, open an issue in the eval-harness repo and tag owners. For onboarding help, contact the applied-ml rotation channel or the model-onboarding team.
